Title: Darul Huda Islamic University: The Niche of Educational Reform in South India
Excerpt: The postulation of Darul Huda Islamic University as an integrated education hub came to form at a time when the most influential Masjid-centralized religious teaching pedagogy gradually deteriorated, and socio-religious values became timid of stable existence of religious education amidst the overwhelming dominance of science and economy. Even though many expert traditional scholars have emerged, the absence of capable personalities to critically engage with modernity and effectively exchange knowledge through innovative methods, transcending the linguistic challenges became a bleak question for many.
Content:
## Intro
The postulation of Darul Huda Islamic University as an integrated education hub came to form at a time when the most influential Masjid-centralized religious teaching pedagogy gradually deteriorated, and socio-religious values became timid of stable existence of religious education amidst the overwhelming dominance of science and economy. Even though many expert traditional scholars have emerged, the absence of capable personalities to critically engage with modernity and effectively exchange knowledge through innovative methods, transcending the linguistic challenges became a bleak question for many.

> Seeking the solution to these challenges paved the way for the establishment of Darul Huda as a new system encompassing all traditional values, yet designed for the reception of practicable reformations. The inauguration of Darul Huda as an outcome of the persistence of Dr. U Bapputty Haji, M.M Basheer Musliyar, and C.H Hydrose Musliyar, the pioneers of Sunni Mahallu Federation, turned out to be a milestone in Kerala model of religious education. It was a herculean task to introduce society to a new model of education that varies from the traditional trajectory they have experienced so far.

## Body
### 1st
The manifestation of Darul Huda education system resolved as much as possible deficiencies that were affecting the prior-integrated curriculum, implemented by M.M Basheer Musliyar at Rahmaniyya Arabic College, Kadameri in early 1970s. Darul Huda envisions a comprehensive methodology that emphasizes acquiring education and the resultant personal development and spiritual purification. The vital objective of this system was to revive the knowledge production that has vanished from the Muslim world for a long time and to create an academic atmosphere where healthy debates and discourses are being held.

### 2nd
Despite the suspicious questioning and critical analyzing of the public towards the significance of such an institution, prayers, and wholehearted support from great visionary scholars such as Sayyid Muhammad Ali Shihab, Shamsul Ulama E.K Abubaker Musliyar and Kottumala Abubaker Musliyar fuelled up the drastic changes in Darul Huda. Standing apart from the traditional scholars whose educational interventions were merely confined to their regional surroundings, the trailblazers of this system dreamt of shaping a scholastic community that perceived efficient knowledge and practical skills to play a key role in knowledge transmission, regardless of regional linguistic limitations. The communal leaders were conscious of the prominence of pervading the ideology of Samastha Kerala Jamiyyathul Ulama all over the nation. Compulsory incorporation of the Urdu language in the syllabus also opened new chances for Islamic propagation and knowledge exchange in various states other than Kerala. Within 40 years of erection, marking its own distinctive position in the knowledge explosion, Darul Huda is progressing radically towards its objective of being peculiar, exhibiting substantial reforms in the whole education system. The institution is eagerly practicalizing innovative methods in both physical infrastructure and technical facilities.

### 3rd
Darul Huda was upgraded to a university in 2009. In due course, Darul Huda acquired its membership in the League of the Islamic Universities, Cairo, and later the Federation of the Universities of the Islamic World, Morocco. Darul Huda's educational system embodies Secondary, Senior Secondary, six departments in Degree and ten in postgraduation, senate, syndicate, academic counsel, and Board of Studies.

### 4th
A national institute was established for non-Keralite students in 1999. The consciousness of leaders, erecting different independent campuses should break the ground for centralizing propagational activities in various states drove them to build off campuses in Northern Karnataka, Assam, Andra Pradesh, Bengal, and Maharashtra.

### 5th
So far, Darul Huda has constituted academic collaboration with more than 12 International Islamic Universities, which include International Islamic University Malaysia, al-Qarawwiyin University of Morocco, Sultan Sharif Ali Islamic University of Bruno, University of Ankara, Turkey, and Islamic University of Rotterdam in the Netherlands. At the same time, National universities such as Jamia Millia, JNU, and Maulana Azad National University have also concurred on the validation of Darul Huda curriculum.As women are supposed to play a major part in social development, courses of Zahrawiyya and Mahdiyya project on moral development and religious discipline of women were established. The chances for understanding Islam regardless of age, and gender limitation, is creatively organized under CPET, (Central for Public Education and Training).

## Conclusion
There are more than 10,000 students on 39 campuses, located both in Kerala and other states. 4250 learners under the public education initiative, and more than 1,00,000 learners in twelve states under Hadia. These instances all denote the fact that about one lakh and more are still acquiring knowledge under Darul Huda and its different initiatives. Divergent proposals under Hadia, the alumni association of Hudawi graduates, including establishing primary educational centres, and Model-Mahallu village, designed for academic, and social empowerment, are on the verge of implementation. It is highly expected that the changes will gradually influence society from the very grassroots levels. Several courses are executed successfully even in non-Arabic countries by Hadia. The institutional management and Hadia are co-acting vigorously to bring off the Darul Huda Model all over the world.

Title: Forty Years of Visionary Education: The Legacy of Darul Huda Islamic University
Content:
The journey of Darul Huda Islamic University (DHIU), from its modest beginnings with limited resources to becoming a globally acclaimed centre of excellence in education and community development, is nothing short of extraordinary. This exceptional educational system emerged during a turbulent period when attempts were made globally to relevantize the Islamic knowledge and education to face the challenges of modernity and westernization in the Muslim countries. Spearheaded by the visionaries like Syed Naqib al-Attas, one such movement was known for its attempt 'Islamize the knowledge and resulted in the establishment of universities like International Islamic University of Malaysia (IIUM). Although Darul Huda is not directly linked to such a global movement, it was also the call of the time to tackle the arduous challenges of the period that resulted in its foundation.

MM Basheeer Musliyar, CH Haidaroos Musliyar and Dr. U. Bapputti Haji were not some western-educated intellectuals coming back to the pathetic realities of their homelands, rather they were the real 'organic intellectuals' who keenly recognized the pressing need for a community of intellectuals equipped with traditional education and secular training, transcending the linguistic boundaries of Kerala. What began as an ambitious idea soon transformed into a cornerstone of educational excellence, proving that "Great things often have small beginnings."

The establishment of Darul Huda was far from a simple task, as it was not just another educational institution. Introducing an integrated education system rooted in traditional Islamic values while incorporating timely pedagogical reforms was a groundbreaking concept for Kerala's conservative Muslim community. So, the founders of Darul Huda had to navigate unchartered waters to turn this innovative vision into reality. Thanks to the unwavering dedication and collaborative efforts of the trio and the visionary pioneers of the Sunni Mahallu Federation, a revolutionary educational model emerged. This "Darul Huda model," originating from South India, not only set a new benchmark for integrated learning but also became a beacon of inspiration for generations to come.

Darul Huda's pedagogical system encompasses a comprehensive structure of lengthy 12 years of rigorous education, including Secondary and Senior Secondary education, six departments at the Degree level, ten departments in Postgraduate studies, as well as its various governing bodies. In 1999, the university took a significant step by establishing a national institute dedicated to non-Keralite students, reflecting its inclusive vision. The farsighted leadership, driven by the ambition to decentralize and amplify empowerment activities across various states, laid the foundation for the establishment of off-campus centres in regions such as Northern Karnataka, Assam, Andhra Pradesh, Bengal and Maharashtra, marking yet another milestone in Darul Huda's mission to broaden its educational and cultural reach.

Recognizing the pivotal role women play in social development, the Zahrawiyya and Mahdiyya programs focus on fostering moral growth and enhancing religious discipline among women. Furthermore, opportunities for understanding Islam, transcending barriers of age and gender, are thoughtfully and creatively structured under the initiative of Centre for Public Education and Training (CPET), ensuring inclusive access to knowledge and empowerment for all.

DHIU's programs range from foundational Islamic studies to advanced research in theology, linguistics, and social sciences. The commitment of the institution to all-round graduates is evident in its emphasis on critical thinking, ethical reasoning, and practical application of knowledge. It is this integrated model that has enabled DHIU to prepare students who excel both as scholars of Islam and as contributors to the broader global community.

Being an Islamic University, Darul Huda places great emphasis on the holistic development of its students, encouraging them to excel not only in academics but also in extracurricular activities. One of the standout initiatives in this regard is the National Art Fest named as "Sibaq", organized in the break of two years for all students across the university's affiliated institutes. This vibrant event serves as an excellent platform for students to showcase their creativity, skills, and talents in various forms of art. Whether it's religious or secular arts, the Art Fest allows students to express themselves, fostering an environment of innovation and self-discovery. By providing such opportunities, Darul Huda ensures that its students grow into well-rounded individuals capable of contributing meaningfully to both cultural and academic spheres.

Beyond an Educational Institute
Now with Darul Huda is celebrating its fortieth anniversary, it's significant to reflect the societal impact it made since its elevation to a university in 2009. When it comes to societal contribution, it would be inappropriate to look beyond Hadia (Hudawis' Association for Devoted Islamic Activities), the alumni organization of Darul Huda Islamic University. But as the union prefers to be called itself, it's more than an alumni association as it is arguably the most constructive union of graduates in Kerala with its unique vision, coordinated action plan and impactful working strategy.

All programs and initiatives under Hadia are meticulously coordinated through the Hadia Centre for Social Excellence (CSE), established in 2015 and located in Panakkad. This dedicated centre of excellence, initiated by Hadia, plays a pivotal role in the upliftment of minorities across India. CSE firmly believes in education as both a catalyst for growth and a solution to the profound challenges faced by these communities. The centre is committed to advancing research and academic studies, taking proactive steps in publishing, actively engaging with media, executing impactful social empowerment projects, developing essential human resources, and fostering the restoration of mental health within society. With a vision to become a beacon of positive transformation, CSE aims to address the complex challenges confronting minorities in India through a holistic, integrated approach. By remaining steadfast in its mission, CSE seeks to make a lasting impact, nurturing growth, empowerment, and overall societal well-being.

As the social and political context of the country demands today, Hadia's National Education Project is extensively focused on the cultural empowerment of underprivileged communities in northern Indian villages with the primary objective of ensuring every Muslim child receives fundamental religious education before adulthood. Launching in 2012 at Darul Huda Andhra Centre, Punkanur, Hadia's National Education Project has established 2500 Hadiya Moral Schools across 14 states impacting the lives of 89,740 students with a dedicated team consisting of 1218 teachers, 56 muftis, and 24 coordinators. Beyond moral schools, Hadia is committed to establish model mahalls and the empowerment of madrassas, contributing to a comprehensive educational strategy.

Drawing inspirations from Hadia's National Education project, Qurtuba Foundation is the recent and evolutionary development which is grounded in values and guided by pursuits of knowledge. As a registered Section 8, not-for-profit organization the Qurtuba Institute of Academic Excellence stands as a symbol of academic distinction and holistic character development. With its unique 10-year program commencing from the 6th grade, the institute places a strong emphasis on language proficiency, moral values, artistic expression, and professional courses. This approach aims to cultivate well-rounded graduates equipped to make meaningful contributions across diverse fields.

Under the umbrella of Qurtuba, Shariat Colleges have significantly enhanced the academic standards of Madrasas in the Seemanchal Region. Offering a structured academic framework, these colleges prepare graduates for careers in teaching, Islamic learning centre administration, leadership in prayer services, and advanced studies in Islamic jurisprudence. This comprehensive program opens doors for students to excel in both spiritual and professional domains.

The Kafil Edu Village initiative is another remarkable program under the foundation which addresses the critical needs of orphans in the Seemanchal Region, providing them with care, education, and accommodation from ages 3 to 18. Younger children are nurtured by widows appointed as caregivers, while older orphans are enrolled in public schools, with all expenses covered by the Kafil Office. This initiative ensures these children are supported and empowered to build promising futures.

In its 40 years of existence, Darul Huda Islamic University has carved a distinctive niche in the realm of education, advancing rapidly toward its goal of transforming the educational landscape. The institution has consistently implemented innovative practices, not only in its academic methodologies but also in its physical and technological infrastructure. In 2009, Darul Huda achieved the significant milestone of being upgraded to a university. Subsequently, it became a member of the League of Islamic Universities in Cairo and the Federation of Universities of the Islamic World in Morocco.

Darul Huda has established academic partnerships with over 12 international Islamic universities, including the International Islamic University Malaysia, Al-Qarawiyyin University in Morocco, Sultan Sharif Ali Islamic University in Brunei, Ankara University in Turkey, and the Islamic University of Rotterdam in the Netherlands. Additionally, prominent national universities such as Jamia Millia Islamia, Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), and Maulana Azad National Urdu University have recognized and validated Darul Huda's curriculum, further enhancing its credibility and reach.

To bring it all together, Darul Huda Islamic University's remarkable journey over the past forty years stands as a testament to its unwavering commitment to education, spiritual growth, and societal development. The university's unique blend of traditional Islamic teachings and contemporary academic disciplines has empowered its students to navigate the complexities of modern life while remaining deeply rooted in their faith and values. As Darul Huda embarks on the next chapter of its journey, it continues to inspire and pave the way for future generations, remaining steadfast in its mission to nurture minds, foster leadership, and contribute to the betterment of society. Truly, the forty years of fulfilment mark not just a milestone, but a continued promise of growth, excellence, and impact for years to come.

Title: Farmer
Content:
They awake as the sun begins to rise,
Perhaps not completing their sleep for us.

They breathe in the fresh, cool morning air,
Then ready themselves to work the fields for us.

We think of progress inside towering buildings,
But they know how their hands can truly save us.

They revel in the pure beauty of nature,
While we harm it, destroying it for us.

They fill their plates with simple, humble fare,
Yet through their hard work, they feed us the best to us.

I can prove this to you—
They are the true hard workers, for us.

Title: Life is Joyful
Content:
Life is meant to be joyful,

Yet so many fall as victims,

 Many suffer under the weight of others—

 But never forget:

Don’t hold back your spring,

Let it unwind,

And embrace the joy within your life.

Life is meant to be joyful.

Sometimes the skies grow dark,

People may scorn your existence.

But don’t waste your precious time—

Honor it,

And savor the joy in your life.

Life is meant to be joyful.

Some burn with envy at your success,

Others may push you away.

But don’t let it dull your spirit.

Hold fast to your dignity,

Use it as your strength,

And find the joy in your life.

Life is meant to be joyful.

Title: Oh! What’s the Winter
Content:
Oh, what a cold day today,

I awoke from sleep,

And saw the mist covering the world.

The grasses are wet with mist,

And the leaves glisten too.

Birds sing songs in the trees.

Oh, what a cold day today.

Mama made tea for us, and we drank it,

But still, the cold remained.

Oh, what a cold day today.

Everyone sleeps under thick blankets,

While I lie awake, watching the mist drift away.

Oh, what a cold day today.


In the evening, we go out to play,

But the cold keeps us from our fun.

Oh, what a cold day today.

At night, we gather around the bonfire,

Seeking relief from the chill.

Oh, what a cold day today.

Title: The Legacy of Godrej: Arjun’s Innovations
Content:
In a small village surrounded by lush fields, a young inventor named Arjun looked up to the Godrej family, whose innovations had transformed countless lives. Inspired by their commitment to quality and community, he set out to create solutions for his own village, where many struggled with agriculture and daily challenges.

Arjun began with the irrigation issue. After months of experimentation, he designed a solar-powered irrigation pump that could easily be installed and operated. This device not only conserved water but also reduced reliance on expensive electric pumps. When he unveiled it to the villagers, their skepticism quickly turned into excitement as they saw how effectively it watered their crops.

Buoyed by this success, Arjun didn’t stop there. He noticed that many villagers faced difficulties in preserving their produce after harvest. He developed a simple solar-powered food dehydrator, allowing families to dry fruits and vegetables, reducing waste and providing nutritious snacks for the off-season.

Word spread about Arjun’s innovations, and soon neighboring villages sought his help. He organized workshops, teaching others to build their own irrigation pumps and dehydrators. The cooperative spirit took hold, and villagers pooled their resources to create a small manufacturing unit. They produced not only Arjun’s inventions but also other eco-friendly tools that promoted sustainable farming.

With increased productivity, the village thrived. Families could afford better education for their children, and local businesses began to flourish. Inspired by his own journey, Arjun launched a mentorship program for the village’s youth, encouraging them to think creatively and find solutions to their own challenges.

As the years passed, Arjun’s impact grew. The village transformed into a hub of innovation, much like the spirit of the Godrej legacy he admired. People traveled from afar to learn about their sustainable practices and inventions.

One day, a representative from the Godrej Group visited the village, intrigued by the stories he had heard. He met Arjun, who shared his journey and the developments that had changed his community. Impressed by his vision and achievements, the representative offered a partnership, helping Arjun expand his innovations beyond the village.

Together, they launched a range of products that blended tradition with modern technology, from eco-friendly farming tools to solar-powered appliances. Arjun’s village became a model for sustainable development, echoing the values of quality, community, and innovation that the Godrej family had long championed.

In the end, Arjun not only honored the legacy of Godrej but also forged a new path for his community, proving that with creativity and collaboration, even the smallest village could shine brightly in the tapestry of progress.

Title: A Degree VS. Deeds: What Makes A Great Teacher
Excerpt: When two friends, Akram and Afzal, interviewed for the same high school teaching job, Akram felt guaranteed to win because he already held a formal B.Ed. degree while Afzal was still waiting for his certification. However, on their way to the interview, they discovered the principal’s young son trapped and crying in some bushes; Akram ignored the boy to head straight to the office, while Afzal rushed to rescue him. Despite scoring lower on the formal written test, Afzal was ultimately hired by the principal, who explained that genuine compassion and a heart for helping students matter far more than what is written on a resume.
Content:
It was a bright and joyful day, with the sun shining at its fullest, inspiring everyone to pursue great things. Two friends, Occurrence and Afzal Akram, were heading to their teaching jobs at the local high school. Both had applied for the position, but only Akram had completed his B.Ed. degree. Afzal, on the other hand, was still waiting for his certification, which he expected to arrive in 20 to 30 days.

Akram, with pride, turned to Afzal and said, "
> I have my B.Ed. degree, Afzal. It's the key to securing this job."

Afzal responded somberly, "
> I don't have it yet. I don't even know if I'll pass the interview without it."

Akram smiled with confidence. "
> It's difficult to offer you a job without the degree, but for me, it will be easy."

After breakfast, they dressed neatly and headed to the city's high school. As they approached the school, they noticed a young boy crying near the bushes. The child was the principal's son, who had somehow gotten stuck in the bushes.

Akram noticed the boy and immediately headed toward the principal's office. Afzal, however, ran to help the child, carefully pulling him out of the bushes.
The principal, who had witnessed everything, ushered them both into his office. "We need to conduct a quick test to evaluate your skills," he said.

Afzal, though not scoring high, answered the questions honestly.

After reviewing their performance, the principal said, "
> Thank you both for coming, but we have decided to go with Afzal for the position."

Akram, surprised and disappointed, asked incredulously, "
> But I have a degree, and he doesn't! Why would you choose him over me?"

The principal's voice was calm but firm. "
> We need teachers who are truly compassionate and helpful, not ones who only care about their own achievements. When my son was stuck in the bushes, you saw him but didn't help. Afzal, however, ran straight to him without hesitation. That's the kind of teacher we want—someone who cares for students, not just their resume."

Akram's face flushed with shame as he realized his mistake. He had been so focused on his qualifications that he failed to see the true value of teaching. With a heavy heart, he left the principal's office and returned home, reflecting on the lesson he had learned that day.
